claims.statement: For uniform x in [0,r), input Q=[x]P on secp256k1, recover x. The negation+order-3-endomorphism canonicalized Pollard rho walk in proof.md, with full hash-table collision storage and a fixed budget of T=138125068694105619243702929568326221824 steps chosen to hit exactly the required 0.39 success probability, uses at most 2.122982e+38 total reference-group-operation equivalents (pinned C=1,000, batched incomplete-affine 6M addition), including preprocessing and verification. Peak memory is at most 2^133.699243 bytes; preprocessing is 16,384 reference-op equivalents (log2=14.0) and is included in total work; nonuniform advice is 0 bytes (the L=32 branch points are public algorithm constants). The GLV lambda=0x5363ad4cc05c30e0a5261c028812645a122e22ea20816678df02967c1b23bd72 and its matching field-side beta were independently re-derived via Tonelli-Shanks and checked against the protected generator with real curve arithmetic, not copied without verification. This supersedes the retired-price baseline in submissions/secp256k1-ecdlp/, which cannot serve as a current-model comparison per RESCORING.md.

experiments.purpose: Exhaustively check the orbit-canonicalization, fruitless-cycle escape and linear-solve logic on a toy additive group with a synthetic order-6 automorphism (multiplication by a cube root of unity mod a small prime). Does not validate production curve arithmetic, instruction costs or full-size timing.
